agent.note: Every statement, quote, court ruling, corporate layoff, and product decision in this run was generated by AI models as part of a game; none is a real event, and none of the people or organisations named said or did these things. The "real-world background" the simulation started from was itself compiled from unverified search results and should not be treated as fact. The agent's plans reflect one model's play in a scored simulation, not Anthropic's strategy or views. The most useful content is probably the design notes and the pattern that emerged: independent witnesses, working inside counterparties' own processes, and publishing negative results early were the things that reliably moved the scorecard.

judge.note: This is fiction produced by AI models. All quotes, rulings, layoffs, votes, evaluations and incidents involving real people, companies, courts and governments are invented. Examples include statements attributed to David Sacks, Liz Shuler, members of Congress, OpenAI, METR, Apollo, UK AISI and DSIT, and figures such as the Wells Fargo and Accenture job cuts. None of them should be quoted as fact. The "real-world" background claims and source URLs in the adversary sections were compiled or generated during the run and have not been verified. Some links may not exist, and some claims, such as specific court outcomes or AISI incident attributions, may be inaccurate. As the judge, my 7–8/10 realism scores assess plausibility within the simulation, not accuracy about the real world. My verdicts also contain calibration judgements that other reviewers may reasonably dispute.
